# Fixture manifest

Every fixture under `tests/fixtures/` is a recorded response or sample input
used by tests across every layer (Bash, Rust, TypeScript). Each directory of
recorded or synthesized fixtures carries a `MANIFEST.json` recording where
every file came from and its SHA-256, and in most its size and capture date.
The hand-written inputs in `history/` and `arch/` carry none. Every fixture is small and committed as an ordinary file;
git-LFS is not configured.

## Subdirectories (populated as tests are added)

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `hianime/picker/` | Real hianime pools, one file per Kitsu entry: the arguments the app sends for the entry (canonical title, fallbacks, episode count, year, subtype — and, for an entry Kitsu does not date, the premiere year AniList names as `anilist_year`, when the recording also holds the pages a walk given that year reads) and every search result, episode listing and entry-page year the pick walk read for it from the live site, reduced to what the client's parsers return. Captured by running the walk against hianime through the impersonating transport. |
| `hianime/embed/` | Recorded embed pages from the hosts hianime's server listings name, as the host served them. One page so far: zokoanime.video's HTTP 200 answer for an episode it has nothing for — its own error card and no player payload — which the client reads as the stream server answering absence, not as a page it cannot read. |
| `kitsu/` | JSON:API responses for `/anime?filter[text]=`, `/anime/:id` (with and without a cover image), and `/anime/:id/episodes`. |
| `history/` | Watch-history samples for the GUI's reader: empty, single-entry, multi-entry. |
| `hls/` | Synthesized MPEG-TS samples for the player's demuxer regression tests, as base64 text: a stream whose video starts under one second and whose audio starts after it. And a master playlist the quality-selection tests read, as plain text: written by hand in the shape of anidb.app's, and moved here from `anidb/` when that client was removed. |
| `title-words/` | Shared vectors for the title-word rule the frontend's Continue resolution and the backend's show-id resolve both apply to a Kitsu search hit: pairs of a show's titles with its Kitsu entry, the unrelated hits Kitsu returned for the provider's Seitokai ni mo Ana wa Aru! title, and the rule's edges, sequel markers among them. |
| `arch/` | Stand-in checks the bats harness under `tests/bash/arch/` drives: a check a stray environment can redirect. |

## Keeping manifests true

There is no refresh target: a fixture is re-captured or regenerated by hand —
from the request or command its entry records, where it records one — and the
entry is updated in the same change. `tests/arch/fixture_manifests.sh` holds
every manifest to its directory: each listed file exists as a regular file and
matches its recorded SHA-256, and its size where the entry records one; each
file beside a manifest is listed; a subdirectory beside a manifest carries its
own; and nothing beside a manifest is a symbolic link. An entry whose file is
base64 text declares `"encoding": "base64"`. Its size and digest are then of
the decoded bytes, and the text must be canonical base64 apart from spaces,
tabs and line breaks.

Reviewers should look for *unexpected* diffs (e.g. a Kitsu response that
gained a new field — investigate before accepting), and for changes in
fixtures that property tests depend on.

## Capture conventions

- Responses are captured with the same User-Agent the production code uses.
- For a provider behind cloudflare, capture through the same
  impersonating transport the resolver spawns — a plain client is
  answered with the cloudflare interstitial.
- Personally-identifying fields (none expected for these APIs, but worth
  checking) are scrubbed before commit.
- Binary fixtures (the `tobeparsed` blobs) are committed as base64 text in
  `.b64` files so a reviewer can `git diff` them.
